questions.question: Q1. Why does a quadcopter require an active electronic control loop to fly level?

answers.a: Because the motors are too weak to lift it without help
answers.b: Because it is open-loop unstable — any small disturbance torque integrates into a tumble unless continuously corrected
answers.c: Because the battery voltage drifts during flight
answers.d: Because the propellers are not balanced

explanations.a: Incorrect — thrust capacity is a separate issue from stability.
explanations.b: Correct — the rigid-body plant is a double integrator, so the vehicle cannot hold attitude on its own; the control loop manufactures the stabilising torque.
explanations.c: Incorrect — voltage sag affects thrust margin, not the fundamental need for feedback.
explanations.d: Incorrect — balance reduces vibration but does not make an unstable plant stable.

questions.question: Q2. In a PID controller, what does the Proportional (K<sub>p</sub>) term contribute?

answers.a: A corrective action proportional to the present error
answers.b: A corrective action proportional to the accumulated past error
answers.c: A corrective action proportional to the rate of change of error
answers.d: A constant bias regardless of error

explanations.a: Correct — the proportional term acts like a spring, producing a restoring effort proportional to how far the present error is from zero.
explanations.b: Incorrect — that describes the integral term.
explanations.c: Incorrect — that describes the derivative term.
explanations.d: Incorrect — a PID term is never independent of the error signal.

questions.question: Q3. What is the main effect of the Derivative (K<sub>d</sub>) term on a control loop?

answers.b: It adds damping, reducing overshoot and oscillation
answers.d: It has no effect on a stable system

explanations.a: Incorrect — eliminating steady-state error is the integral term's job.
explanations.b: Correct — the derivative term reacts to how fast the error is changing, acting as electronic damping that calms overshoot.
explanations.c: Incorrect — it does not change the DC gain.
explanations.d: Incorrect — derivative action strongly shapes the transient response.

questions.question: Q4. Which controller term is responsible for driving steady-state error to exactly zero?

answers.d: None — steady-state error can never be removed

explanations.a: Incorrect — proportional control leaves a finite residual error against a constant disturbance.
explanations.b: Incorrect — the derivative term shapes the transient, not the steady state.
explanations.c: Correct — the integral term keeps accumulating error and injecting effort until the error is exactly zero.
explanations.d: Incorrect — integral action removes constant steady-state error entirely.

questions.question: Q5. The damping ratio ζ of a second-order system is 0.4. How would its step response be described?

answers.b: Critically damped — fastest with no overshoot
answers.c: Underdamped — overshoots and oscillates before settling

explanations.c: Correct — 0 < ζ < 1 is underdamped: the response overshoots and rings before settling.

questions.question: Q6. What does a MEMS gyroscope directly measure, and what is its main weakness for attitude estimation?

answers.a: Absolute tilt angle; weakness is slow response
answers.b: Angular rate; weakness is that integrating it lets a small bias drift without bound
answers.c: Linear acceleration; weakness is temperature sensitivity

explanations.a: Incorrect — a gyro does not read absolute angle directly.
explanations.b: Correct — a gyro measures angular rate; obtaining angle requires integration, which accumulates the bias into unbounded drift.

questions.question: Q7. Why can an accelerometer estimate tilt, and what corrupts that estimate on a flying drone?

answers.a: It senses the gravity vector; vibration and motion noise corrupt it
answers.b: It senses angular rate; bias corrupts it
answers.c: It senses air pressure; wind corrupts it
answers.d: It senses rotation speed; temperature corrupts it

explanations.a: Correct — the accelerometer senses the gravity direction (giving an absolute, drift-free tilt) but motor vibration and translational acceleration add heavy noise.
explanations.d: Incorrect — that is closer to a gyroscope.

questions.question: Q8. What is the purpose of a complementary (or Kalman) filter in a flight controller?

answers.b: To fuse complementary sensors so each covers the other's weakness, yielding one clean estimate
answers.c: To filter the PWM output to the ESCs

explanations.a: Incorrect — it is an estimation filter, not a power amplifier.
explanations.b: Correct — it blends the drift-free-but-noisy accelerometer with the smooth-but-drifting gyro to produce a single accurate attitude estimate.
explanations.c: Incorrect — that is unrelated signal conditioning.
explanations.d: Incorrect — voltage regulation is a power-electronics task.

questions.question: Q9. In the Ziegler–Nichols method, what is the 'ultimate gain' K<sub>u</sub>?

answers.a: The maximum gain the hardware can physically output
answers.b: The proportional gain at which the loop oscillates with constant (sustained) amplitude
answers.c: The gain that gives zero overshoot
answers.d: The gain at which the motor saturates

explanations.a: Incorrect — it is a property of the control loop, not a hardware output limit.
explanations.b: Correct — K<sub>u</sub> is the proportional gain at the stability boundary, where the response is a sustained constant-amplitude oscillation.
explanations.c: Incorrect — at K<sub>u</sub> the system is marginally stable, far from zero overshoot.
explanations.d: Incorrect — saturation is a hardware nonlinearity, not the ultimate gain.

questions.question: Q10. How does a larger, heavier airframe (higher moment of inertia J) affect the attitude response for the same PID gains?

answers.b: It responds more slowly — higher inertia lowers the natural frequency
answers.c: Inertia has no effect on the control response

explanations.a: Incorrect — more inertia resists angular acceleration, slowing the response.
explanations.b: Correct — since ω<sub>n</sub> = √(K<sub>p</sub>/J), a larger J lowers the natural frequency and slows the loop, usually requiring higher gains.
explanations.c: Incorrect — inertia is central to the plant dynamics.
explanations.d: Incorrect — higher inertia does not by itself cause instability.
